questions.text: The cut-off price in a book-built issue means:
options: Lowest price bid by any investor
Highest price at which all shares can be allotted
questions.explanation: Cut-off price is the price at which the total demand matches the shares available for issue.

questions.text: Which asset class is generally considered most suitable for capital preservation with modest returns over the short term?
options: Structured products linked to equity indices
questions.explanation: Liquid and short-term debt instruments usually focus on capital preservation and modest returns.

questions.text: The main contribution of Modern Portfolio Theory is that it:
options: Quantified diversification using covariance or correlation between assets
questions.explanation: MPT quantified diversification benefits using statistical tools like covariance and correlation to manage risk.

questions.text: Under SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996, a mutual fund is constituted as:
questions.explanation: Every mutual fund is set up as a trust under the Indian Trusts Act, 1882, with the sponsor, trustees, and AMC as constituents.

questions.text: Which loan normally carries floating interest rate linked to external benchmark?
questions.explanation: Most home loans today are linked to RBI’s repo or MCLR rate.

questions.text: Investing in art, paintings and collectibles is generally categorised as:
questions.explanation: Art and collectibles are considered alternative investments—illiquid, specialised and often suitable only for sophisticated investors.

questions.text: Under SEBI rules, an AMC can offer:
options: Both a value fund and a contra fund
Only a value fund but not a contra fund
Only a contra fund but not a value fund
Either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both
questions.explanation: A mutual fund house can have either a value fund or a contra fund, but not both, as per SEBI categorisation norms.

questions.text: From an advisory perspective, why is understanding different asset classes important?
options: To match assets with client’s goals, risk profile and time horizon
To help the client avoid diversification
To recommend only one product to all clients
questions.explanation: Advisers must understand asset characteristics to recommend suitable portfolios aligned to each client’s goals and risk tolerance.

questions.text: Book building is used to:
options: Fix the face value of shares
Determine issue price based on investor bids
questions.explanation: Book building is a process of price discovery in IPOs where investors bid within a price band.

questions.text: From an ethics perspective, disclosure of all fees and charges should be:
options: Clear, prominent, and in writing before engagement
questions.explanation: Clients must clearly know the full cost structure upfront to make informed decisions.

questions.text: Which of the following complaints is typically NOT handled through SCORES?
questions.explanation: SCORES addresses regulatory or procedural violations; mere dissatisfaction with performance does not qualify.

questions.text: The key compliance requirement for all intermediaries under SEBI is:
options: Filing annual audit reports with SEBI
Maintaining client confidentiality and proper records
questions.explanation: Intermediaries must maintain confidentiality and records as part of SEBI’s code of conduct and inspection norms.

questions.text: The nominal rate of interest is 12% p.a. compounded monthly. The effective annual rate (EAR) is closest to:
If correlation between two assets is -1, then portfolio risk can be:
options: Equal to average of the two risks
questions.explanation: Perfect negative correlation (-1) means movements offset each other, potentially eliminating portfolio risk.

questions.text: Category I AIFs generally invest in:
questions.explanation: Category I AIFs include venture-capital, SME, social-venture and infrastructure funds that create positive economic impact.

questions.text: Rematerialisation of mutual fund units refers to:
options: Converting demat units into physical statement form
questions.explanation: Rematerialisation means converting electronic demat holdings into physical statement form, usually to hold directly with AMC.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about asset allocation is TRUE?
options: It has minimal impact on portfolio performance
It is the key determinant of long-term portfolio returns and risk
It focuses only on stock selection
It can be ignored once the portfolio is constructed
questions.explanation: Empirical studies show asset allocation is the major driver of a portfolio’s long-term risk and return.

questions.text: Stop-loss orders are mainly used to:
options: Limit potential losses by triggering a market/limit order when price reaches a specified level
questions.explanation: Stop-loss orders help investors restrict downside risk beyond a point.

questions.text: Savings ratio is defined as:
questions.explanation: It measures the proportion of income saved each year.

questions.text: Holders of equity shares are known as:
questions.explanation: Equity shareholders are owners and have residual claims on assets and profits.

questions.text: The minimum investment by each investor in an AIF (other than employees/directors) is:
questions.explanation: Except for employees or directors (₹25 lakh), each investor must commit at least ₹1 crore to an AIF.

questions.text: For a young investor with long investment horizon and high risk appetite, which allocation tilt is generally appropriate?
options: Higher allocation to equity and growth-oriented assets
Only bank FDs and government bonds
questions.explanation: Long horizon and high risk appetite usually justify a higher allocation to equity and growth assets.

questions.text: In a plain vanilla bond, the main intrinsic features are:
options: Coupon rate, maturity and principal (face value)
questions.explanation: A basic bond is defined by its coupon rate, its maturity (tenor) and its principal or face value that is repaid at maturity.

questions.text: If monthly expenses are ₹60,000 and liquid assets ₹2,40,000, the liquidity ratio equals:
Dynamic bond funds:
options: Maintain a fixed portfolio duration at all times
Can move across different durations based on interest rate view
Invest only in government securities of 10-year maturity
questions.explanation: Dynamic bond funds actively manage duration and credit exposure, shifting across maturities according to the fund manager’s interest rate outlook.

questions.text: Current yield of a bond is:
options: Annual coupon divided by current market price
Annual coupon divided by face value
Yield to maturity divided by price
questions.explanation: Current yield = annual coupon / current market price, ignoring capital gains or losses.

questions.text: From an adviser’s perspective, suitability of equity for a client depends on:
options: Risk tolerance, time horizon and financial goals
questions.explanation: Suitability assessment considers risk appetite, time horizon and objectives, not merely income or administrative details.

questions.text: A 'risk-seeking' investor is one who:
options: Engages willingly in fair games with uncertain outcomes
questions.explanation: Risk-seeking investors make an upward adjustment to utility for risk, willingly engaging in fair games.

questions.text: Cut-off timings in mutual funds primarily ensure:
options: Fairness and uniformity in determining which day’s NAV is applicable
Higher returns for early morning investors
That only institutional investors can transact
questions.explanation: Cut-off timings standardise which day’s NAV is applied to a transaction, ensuring fairness and no preferential treatment.

questions.text: In PV = FV / (1 + r)ⁿ, 'n' refers to:
questions.explanation: ‘n’ is the number of compounding periods.

questions.text: Bonus shares are issued:
options: For raising new capital from investors
Out of free reserves or retained earnings to existing shareholders
To employees as part of ESOPs
questions.explanation: Bonus shares are issued by capitalising reserves and giving additional shares to existing shareholders.

questions.text: Equity Linked Savings Schemes (ELSS) must invest at least how much of their portfolio in equity securities?
questions.explanation: ELSS schemes must hold at least 80% of their portfolio in equity securities and offer tax deduction under Section 80C under the old tax regime.

questions.text: In case of transmission without nomination, the claimant must provide:
questions.explanation: For non-nominated cases, claimant must provide a death certificate, legal heir certificate, or notarized will copy.

questions.text: The formula to calculate EMI is:
questions.explanation: EMI = P r (1+r)^n / ((1+r)^n − 1), where P=principal, r=periodic rate, n=number of periods.

questions.text: To accumulate ₹10 lakh in 15 years at 9% p.a., the annual deposit required is approximately:
questions.explanation: Using FV of annuity formula, deposit ≈ 36,000 per year.

questions.text: Under PMS regulations, the minimum investment amount per client is:
questions.explanation: SEBI mandates a minimum investment of ₹50 lakh for investors availing Portfolio Management Services.

questions.text: Portfolio risk depends on:
options: Variances and covariances between all assets in the portfolio
questions.explanation: Portfolio risk depends not just on the variance of each asset but also on their covariance or correlation.

questions.text: All else equal, which bond will have the highest duration?
options: Floating rate bond with frequent resets
questions.explanation: Longer maturity and lower coupons push more cash flows into the distant future, increasing duration and interest rate sensitivity.

questions.text: Which budgeting method allocates funds first to essential expenses and savings before discretionary spending?
questions.explanation: Pay-yourself-first ensures savings are prioritised before optional spending.

questions.text: In the investor life cycle, the 'accumulation phase' is characterized by:
options: High net worth and focus on capital preservation
Building assets with higher risk tolerance and long horizon
questions.explanation: In the accumulation phase, investors are early in their careers, taking higher risk to build wealth over a long horizon.

questions.text: An investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented by:
options: Number of shares of the AMC
Number of bonds issued by the scheme
Number of units of the scheme
Amount of cash in the trust account
questions.explanation: Each investor’s holding in a mutual fund is represented in terms of units of the scheme.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, investor complaints must be redressed within:
questions.explanation: Intermediaries are expected to resolve investor grievances within 30 days of receipt.

questions.text: “Investment-grade” debt generally refers to:
options: Debt rated in the lower categories indicating high default risk
Debt with credit ratings in higher categories indicating relatively lower default risk
Debt that has no rating but is issued by start-ups
Any government bond irrespective of rating
questions.explanation: Investment-grade ratings indicate relatively lower default risk compared to non–investment grade or ‘junk’ ratings.

questions.text: Which type of investor is MOST suitable for complex structured products and distressed securities?
options: Investor with low risk tolerance and short horizon
Beginner investor just starting with savings
Sophisticated / HNI investor who understands risks
Investor who wants guaranteed principal protection
questions.explanation: Complex and high-risk products are generally meant for sophisticated investors who understand potential losses.

questions.text: Portfolios below the efficient frontier are:
options: Sub-optimal as they offer lower return for a given risk
questions.explanation: Portfolios below the efficient frontier are inefficient because they offer less return for the same risk level.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly describes ‘Direct Access Facility’ in PMS?
options: A service allowing investors to transact through distributors
A feature enabling investors to invest directly without intermediaries
A regulatory exemption from SEBI registration
A facility allowing mutual fund investors to switch to PMS
questions.explanation: Under the direct access facility, investors can invest directly in PMS without intermediaries, reducing cost.

questions.text: Complaints related to the National Pension System (NPS) are handled by:
options: PFRDA and the Central Recordkeeping Agency (CRA)
questions.explanation: PFRDA and its designated CRA handle NPS-related complaints through their grievance redress mechanism.

questions.text: A decrease in net worth may be due to:
questions.explanation: Borrowing or fall in asset values can reduce net worth.

questions.text: As the number of securities in a portfolio increases, the number of covariance terms:
questions.explanation: For n securities, the number of covariance terms is n(n–1)/2, which grows rapidly as portfolio size increases.

questions.text: In the context of personal finance, risk tolerance refers to:
options: The ability to pay income tax
The client’s willingness to accept fluctuations in investment value
The number of bank accounts held
questions.explanation: Risk tolerance is about the psychological comfort with volatility and the possibility of loss.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of mis-selling?
options: Explaining all risks clearly before sale
Selling a product unsuitable for the client’s risk profile to earn higher commission
questions.explanation: Mis-selling includes pushing unsuitable products mainly to earn higher commissions, ignoring client needs and risk profile.

questions.text: The sequence in which mutual fund units are held jointly determines:
options: The tax liability of each holder
Whose signature is required for redemption
questions.explanation: The sequence determines signature order, redemption rights, and nomination applicability for joint holders.

questions.text: Effective grievance redress mechanisms help in:
options: Improving investor trust and market integrity
questions.explanation: Robust grievance redress systems improve investor confidence, reduce disputes, and enhance market integrity.

questions.text: The primary regulator for mutual funds in India is:
options: Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI)
Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI)
questions.explanation: SEBI regulates mutual funds under the SEBI (Mutual Funds) Regulations, 1996 and subsequent amendments.

questions.text: Which of the following is the BEST example of a financial investment asset?
options: Gold jewellery used for personal wear
Equity shares of a listed company
questions.explanation: Equity shares are a financial investment asset. Gold jewellery and personal-use assets are primarily consumption assets, not pure financial investments.

questions.text: Portfolio Managers must report performance:
options: Uniformly across disclosure documents, marketing materials, and client reports
questions.explanation: Performance must be disclosed uniformly across all communications, as per SEBI’s performance disclosure norms.

questions.text: Permanent Account Number (PAN) is mandatory for all mutual fund investments except when:
options: Aggregate investment is up to ₹50,000 per year under Micro SIPs
questions.explanation: SEBI exempts Micro SIP investors (aggregate ≤ ₹50,000 per financial year) from mandatory PAN if other KYC norms are met.

questions.text: In a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP), the main benefit arising from investing a fixed amount at regular intervals is called:
questions.explanation: SIPs enable rupee cost averaging, where the investor buys more units when prices are low and fewer when prices are high, reducing average cost per unit over time.

questions.text: Long-term financial goals generally relate to:
options: Events to be funded in more than 5 years
questions.explanation: Long-term goals, such as retirement planning or funding children’s higher education, typically have a horizon of more than 5 years.

questions.text: Which of these is a good example of a SMART goal?
options: I want to be rich someday
I will save whatever is left at month end
I will invest ₹10,000 per month for 10 years to accumulate ₹20 lakh for my child’s education
I want to reduce my expenses
questions.explanation: SMART goals are Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound; option C satisfies these criteria.

questions.text: The bond market is also known as:
questions.explanation: Bond or debt market deals with fixed-income securities like bonds and debentures.

questions.text: The formula for the Sharpe Ratio is:
options: (Portfolio Return – Risk-Free Rate) / Standard Deviation of Portfolio
questions.explanation: Sharpe Ratio = (Rp – Rf) / σp, where Rp is portfolio return, Rf is risk-free rate, and σp is portfolio’s standard deviation.

questions.text: The SEBI (Research Analyst) Regulations were notified in:
questions.explanation: SEBI introduced the Research Analyst Regulations in 2014 to regulate research dissemination and prevent conflicts of interest.

questions.text: Future value of an annuity of ₹10,000 p.a. for 5 years at 10% p.a. will be (approx.):
Capital appreciation in equity investments arises from:
options: Increase in market price of shares over time
questions.explanation: Equity investors gain from share price appreciation when the company grows in profitability and value.

questions.text: Debt consolidation is a strategy to:
options: Merge multiple loans into one with better terms
questions.explanation: Combining debts reduces complexity and can lower interest burden.

questions.text: Which statement about personal financial planning is TRUE?
options: It is a one-time exercise done at the start of a career
It needs periodic review and updating as life circumstances change
It only applies to high-net-worth individuals
It is relevant only close to retirement
questions.explanation: Financial planning is a dynamic process and needs regular review as income, family situation and goals change.

questions.text: Benchmarking a portfolio is useful because it:
options: Removes the need for risk analysis
Provides a standard for performance comparison
questions.explanation: A benchmark represents a relevant market index or combination of indices used to evaluate portfolio performance.

questions.text: Account Aggregators in India:
options: Collect and share financial data based on customer consent
questions.explanation: Account Aggregators are RBI-licensed entities that aggregate and share financial data securely with consent.

questions.text: Under SEBI regulations, AMCs must disclose the number of investor complaints received:
options: Monthly on their websites and to AMFI
questions.explanation: AMCs disclose monthly complaint statistics on their websites and to AMFI for transparency.

questions.text: If an amount doubles in 9 years, the approximate annual compound rate is:
questions.explanation: Rule of 72 ⇒ 72 ÷ 9 = 8%; more precisely 7.9%.

questions.text: If ₹1,00,000 is invested for 2 years at 10% p.a. simple interest, the total amount at maturity will be:
Which of the following is NOT a typical money market instrument in India?
questions.explanation: A 10-year G-Sec is a long-term dated security; the others are classic money market instruments with maturities up to one year.

questions.text: AMFI primarily functions as:
options: A mutual fund industry self-regulatory organization (SRO)
questions.explanation: The Association of Mutual Funds in India (AMFI) is an SRO promoting investor awareness and ethical conduct among mutual funds.

questions.text: An option is said to be 'in the money' when:
options: The holder has not paid the premium
The option would yield a positive payoff if exercised immediately
questions.explanation: An in-the-money option has intrinsic value; exercising it immediately would generate a gain for the holder.

questions.text: Which of the following is consistent with fair dealing among clients?
options: Allocating investment opportunities equitably without unfair preference
Sharing one client’s strategy with another without consent
questions.explanation: Fair dealing means treating all clients fairly and equitably, without unfair preference or discrimination.

questions.text: If the compounding frequency increases from annual to quarterly, the effective annual rate (EAR):
questions.explanation: More frequent compounding increases the effective annual rate.

questions.text: The role of a financial planner primarily includes:
options: Helping clients articulate goals, preparing the plan and guiding implementation
questions.explanation: Planners focus on understanding goals, designing strategies and supporting implementation; they cannot guarantee returns.

questions.text: From an ethical standpoint, client complaints should be viewed as:
options: Opportunities to improve processes and trust
questions.explanation: Complaints help identify gaps and improve service quality; handling them fairly builds long-term trust.

questions.text: Which of the following return measures eliminates the effect of external cash flows?
questions.explanation: Time-weighted return neutralizes the impact of deposits and withdrawals, accurately reflecting portfolio manager performance.

questions.text: Portfolio Management Services (PMS) in India are regulated under:
questions.explanation: Portfolio Management Services are governed by SEBI (Portfolio Managers) Regulations, 2020, which replaced the earlier 1993 regulations.

questions.text: Which of the following correctly pairs derivative type and user intent?
options: Option – limited loss for buyer; Future – symmetrical gains and losses
questions.explanation: Futures expose both sides to full price movement; option buyers have limited loss potential.

questions.text: The most widely used risk-adjusted performance measure is:
questions.explanation: The Sharpe Ratio is the most popular risk-adjusted performance measure, assessing excess return per unit of total risk.

questions.text: If discretionary spending rises sharply, the likely outcome is:
options: Reduced surplus and possible debt increase
questions.explanation: Overspending reduces savings and may require borrowing.

questions.text: Which of these steps helps avoid a debt trap?
options: Using credit cards for minimum payment only
questions.explanation: Emergency funds reduce reliance on borrowing during financial stress.

questions.text: A callable bond is one where:
options: The investor can redeem early at a predetermined price
The issuer has the right to redeem the bond before maturity
The coupon rate changes automatically with inflation
The bond has no maturity date
questions.explanation: Callable bonds give the issuer the right to redeem the bond prematurely, usually when interest rates fall, increasing reinvestment risk for investors.

questions.text: Dematerialisation refers to:
options: Conversion of physical share certificates into electronic form
questions.explanation: Dematerialisation converts paper share certificates into electronic holdings in a demat account.

questions.text: The ‘hurdle rate’ in a PMS refers to:
options: The minimum return required before profit-sharing fees apply
questions.explanation: The hurdle rate is the minimum return the PMS must achieve before charging performance fees.

questions.text: Which of the following investors are eligible to invest in AIFs?
options: Resident, NRI and foreign investors, subject to FEMA
questions.explanation: AIFs can accept investment from resident, NRI and foreign investors in compliance with FEMA and SEBI norms.

questions.text: Which of these tools is commonly used for tracking personal expenses?
questions.explanation: Bank and card statements help track spending categories.

questions.case_text: Priya and Kunal earn ₹10 lakh and ₹14 lakh per year respectively. They invest in ELSS and NPS and pay home loan interest of ₹3 lakh annually. They want to use Sections 80C, 80CCD, and 24(b).

questions.case_text: Amit and Neha, both aged 30, earn ₹1,00,000 per month jointly. They wish to buy a house worth ₹60 lakh in 5 years and also start saving for retirement at 60. Their current savings are ₹5 lakh invested in bank FDs. They can save ₹25,000 per month. Inflation is 6% p.a.

questions.text: Which of the following is Amit and Neha’s short-term goal?
questions.explanation: Emergency fund (3–6 months expenses) is short-term.

questions.text: Buying the house in 5 years is best categorised as a:
questions.explanation: Goals 3–7 years away are medium-term.

questions.text: Retirement planning is a ______ goal.
questions.explanation: Retirement lies 30 years ahead — a long-term goal.

questions.text: Their total monthly saving rate is:
To beat inflation over long term, they should allocate more to:
questions.explanation: Equities have potential to outperform inflation over long horizons.

questions.case_text: Nisha has three loans — car loan ₹5 lakh at 11%, personal loan ₹3 lakh at 13%, and credit card outstanding ₹1 lakh at 36%. She considers consolidating them into a single loan at 12% for 4 years.

questions.text: Which loan has the highest rate?
Total current outstanding debt:
Proposed consolidated loan rate:
Main advantage of consolidation:

questions.case_text: Meera and Karan have a 10-year-old son and plan to save for his higher education, which they estimate will cost ₹25 lakh in 8 years. They can invest ₹20,000 per month in a balanced mutual fund expected to yield 9% per annum.

questions.text: Estimated goal cost is:

questions.case_text: Arjun, aged 41, was laid off recently. He has ₹12 lakh in savings and spends ₹75,000 monthly. He has no EMIs and expects new employment within 10 months.

questions.text: Current monthly expenses:
Liquid savings available:
Months he can manage without income:

questions.case_text: Rohit plans to buy a sedan costing ₹14 lakh. His bank offers a 5-year vehicle loan at 9% interest. He can either take the loan or use his mutual fund investments currently earning 6.5% p.a.

Loan rate offered:
Investment earning rate:

questions.case_text: Meera plans for her son’s college in 10 years costing ₹30 lakh. She invests ₹18,000 per month at 10% annual return.
